children: was on track to extend its gains to the seventh straight session on Tuesday as the stock rose 1.58% to $598.42 during afternoon trading.
Since October 2, the stock has closed in the green in every session until October 9, during which period MA gained over 6%. Year to date, it has inched up 3.72%, lagging the S&P 500's 14.11% rise.

Seeking Alpha’s quant rating has rated the stock a Hold. Mastercard has been graded an A+ for profitability but an F for valuation. On the other hand, Seeking Alpha analysts have a Buy rating on the stock, with Wall Street even more optimistic with a Strong Buy rating.

rated the stock as Buy, noting that its core payments business remains strong, with healthy volume growth, resilient cross-border activity, and continued operating leverage, but the setup is no longer attractive enough to justify aggressive buying, the analyst added.

“Today, the setup is less explosive but still attractive: Mastercard is back around fair value, the core business remains strong, VAS is still compounding at a high rate, and AI and stablecoins add upside without being necessary for the thesis. I therefore maintain my Buy rating, although I would not chase the stock aggressively at current levels,” Cyn Research said.
Another analyst Millenial Dividends was also bullish on the stock but said that it preferred Mastercard’s competitor Visa for its embedded US exposure, margin superiority, and steadier earnings.

“My personal preference for Visa is because I see the company as more embedded in the US economy, a better inflationary hedge through exposure to non-discretionary spending, and having an adjusted net margin of 54% vs. Mastercard's 48%,” the analyst noted.

title: Mastercard on track to widen gains to seventh straight session
